This bill is part of a package that would introduce an industry funding model for ASIC starting on 1 July 2017.
The package would require ASIC to annually explain its regulatory priorities, resource allocation, and improve its data collection from financial entities.
The government estimates the package would add $308.7 million to the budget over four years and increase compliance costs by $21.1 million each year.
Introduce an industry funding model for ASIC.
Require ASIC to report annually on its regulatory priorities and resource use.
Require ASIC to collect and use more data from financial entities.

The ASIC Supervisory Cost Recovery Levy (Collection) Bill 2017 was introduced to implement an industry funding model requiring all ASIC-regulated entities to pay levies offsetting regulatory costs. Unpaid levies attract 20 per cent annual penalty interest, mandatory activity reporting is required with failure to report an offence, and dishonest reporting incurs a shortfall penalty of twice the levy avoided.

The ASIC Supervisory Cost Recovery Levy (Consequential Amendments) Bill 2017 introduces an industry funding model for ASIC, requiring annual publication of regulatory costs and empowering ASIC to take administrative action against entities that fail to pay levies or penalties within a year. The bill also abolishes the existing market supervision cost recovery regime from 1 July 2017.
